scenario: Read the API root response
steps: Send GET / to the isolated QA backend.
test data: No test data.
expected result: Code returns status success and an application-name message; execution result remains unmeasured.

scenario: Read the health response
steps: Send GET /health to the isolated QA backend.
test data: No test data.
expected result: Code returns status healthy; execution result remains unmeasured.

scenario: Create a new QA user without trusted role or department assignment
steps: POST a JSON body with a valid email, full name, and password to /api/v1/auth/signup; optionally include client-supplied role and department to verify they are ignored.
test data: Unique QA email; disposable password; attempted role=admin and department=Engineering.
expected result: Public signup creates role=user and department=General regardless of client-supplied assignment values; UserResponse excludes password.

scenario: Signup with malformed email
steps: POST signup JSON containing an invalid email.
test data: Unique invalid email such as not-an-email; otherwise valid fields.
expected result: Pydantic EmailStr validation should reject malformed email with HTTP 422; execution remains unmeasured.

scenario: Omit a required signup field
steps: POST signup JSON omitting email, full_name, or password, one field per attempt.
test data: QA payload with one required property omitted each time.
expected result: Pydantic should reject each missing required property with HTTP 422; execution remains unmeasured.

scenario: Register the same email twice
steps: Create a QA account, then repeat signup with that email.
test data: Same unique test email for both requests.
expected result: Second request should return HTTP 400 and detail Email already registered.

scenario: Enter a password below the client-side minimum
steps: Open /signup, enter valid name and email, enter a password shorter than six characters, then submit.
test data: QA-only identity and a five-character password.
expected result: The frontend schema requires at least six characters and should show its validation message without a valid signup submission.

scenario: Log in with a registered QA account
steps: POST form-encoded username and password to /api/v1/auth/login.
test data: Email and password created by TC-003.
expected result: Response code returns access_token, bearer token_type, and user fields; execution remains unmeasured.

scenario: Attempt login with a wrong password
steps: POST form-encoded login using an existing QA email and wrong password.
test data: Existing QA email; deliberately incorrect password.
expected result: Route should return HTTP 401 with detail Invalid email or password.

scenario: Submit login fields as JSON instead of form data
steps: POST JSON containing username and password to /api/v1/auth/login.
test data: QA credentials in JSON body.
expected result: Login declares OAuth2PasswordRequestForm; JSON is not its documented request format and should not authenticate; capture actual HTTP response.

scenario: Call current-user endpoint without a token
steps: Send GET /api/v1/auth/me without Authorization header.
test data: No token.
expected result: OAuth2 bearer dependency should reject the request with HTTP 401.

scenario: Call current-user endpoint with valid token
steps: Login, then send GET /api/v1/auth/me with the returned bearer token.
test data: Token and QA account from TC-003 and TC-008.
expected result: Response should identify the logged-in user and include id, email, full_name, department, and role.

scenario: Use a token after its expiration time
steps: In an isolated QA process configured before startup with ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES=1, log in, wait until after token expiry, then call /api/v1/auth/me.
test data: Disposable QA account; one-minute QA-only expiry setting.
expected result: Token creation adds an exp claim and decode rejects expired tokens; /me should return HTTP 401. Do not change production settings.

scenario: Use a token with an altered signature
steps: Obtain a QA token, alter a character in its signature locally, and call /api/v1/auth/me.
test data: Disposable QA token only; do not use another person's token.
expected result: JWT decoding should reject the altered token and /me should return HTTP 401.

scenario: Submit an invalid token to the verification route
steps: Request GET /api/v1/auth/verify-token/{token} with a clearly invalid QA token value.
test data: Non-secret invalid token string.
expected result: Route should return a response with message Invalid token; its implementation returns this message rather than raising an HTTP error.

scenario: Log out and inspect local session state
steps: Log in through the UI, select Logout or Logout Account in the dashboard layout, then inspect localStorage in the isolated QA browser.
test data: Disposable QA account; isolated browser profile.
expected result: DashboardLayout calls AuthContext logout and navigates to /login; logout removes token, access_token, and user keys. Verify behavior in an actual run.

scenario: Attempt cross-department list, search, and RAG access
steps: Authenticate as a QA user in one department; request list, search, and RAG data for a different department.
test data: Synthetic users and non-sensitive department-specific documents.
expected result: The backend uses the authenticated user's department; conflicting filters are rejected and must not return cross-department content.

scenario: Upload without an authenticated session
steps: Send a harmless supported QA file to POST /api/v1/upload/document without an Authorization header.
test data: Small synthetic TXT file; isolated QA backend only.
expected result: The request is rejected with HTTP 401 and no file or document record is created.

requirement: REQ-DOC-01: List documents in authenticated scope
scenario: List documents without a department filter
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and call GET /api/v1/upload/documents after creating records in multiple departments.
test data: QA records in General and Engineering; user assigned to General.
expected result: The response contains only records in the authenticated user's department, ordered by descending id.

scenario: Filter the list within or outside the authenticated scope
steps: Authenticate as a QA user; request the user's department, then request a different department.
test data: Synthetic user and documents in General and Engineering.
expected result: A matching department filter returns only the user's department; a conflicting filter is rejected and cannot widen access.

requirement: REQ-DEPT-01: All-department filter cannot widen scope
scenario: Request department=All as a regular user
steps: Authenticate as a regular QA user and call GET /api/v1/upload/documents?department=All.
test data: QA records in multiple departments.
expected result: The request is rejected or remains constrained to the authenticated department; it never returns all departments.

scenario: Attempt cross-department document access, deletion, and same-name upload collision
steps: Authenticate as a QA user; target another department's document by list/search/RAG filters and by document ID for deletion; upload a same-named fixture from another department.
test data: Synthetic users and department-specific documents with a disposable file.
expected result: Cross-department data is not returned; deletion is denied before file, vector, or database changes occur; uploading a same-named file does not overwrite another department's stored file.

scenario: Submit upload without file field
steps: POST multipart form to /api/v1/upload/document without file.
test data: No file field.
expected result: FastAPI should reject the missing required UploadFile field with HTTP 422.

scenario: Upload a non-empty TXT QA document in the authenticated department
steps: Authenticate as a QA user assigned to Engineering and upload a multipart TXT file to /api/v1/upload/document.
test data: Valid bearer token; synthetic UTF-8 TXT containing unique, non-sensitive searchable text.
expected result: Code accepts .txt, assigns the authenticated user's department, extracts text, chunks it, stores metadata, and returns document/status/preview/chunk count; verify each returned field.

requirement: REQ-UPLOAD-01: PDF and DOCX document ingestion
scenario: Upload a non-empty PDF and DOCX in separate requests
steps: Upload one small valid PDF and one small valid DOCX to the isolated backend.
test data: Synthetic documents with short, unique text.
expected result: Code has PDF and DOCX extraction paths; each response should include its document and extracted-text/chunk fields; inspect actual status.

scenario: Upload a .doc file and inspect extracted text
steps: Upload a harmless .doc QA fixture and inspect status, preview, and chunk count.
test data: Synthetic legacy DOC document only.
expected result: Extension is allow-listed, but the inspected extraction service has no dedicated .doc parser and falls back to text reading; successful extraction is UNVERIFIED.

scenario: Upload a file with an unsupported extension
steps: POST a harmless .csv-named file to the upload endpoint.
test data: Synthetic CSV with no sensitive contents.
expected result: Extension validation should return HTTP 400 before saving the file.

scenario: Upload a zero-byte TXT file
steps: Upload an empty .txt fixture.
test data: Zero-byte synthetic TXT.
expected result: Code sets status Empty Text and creates zero chunks; verify response and resulting record in QA database.

scenario: Check the displayed upload-size claim
steps: Select a synthetic file larger than 25 MB in the upload UI, without submitting it to a shared or production service; inspect picker/dropzone behavior.
test data: Synthetic file larger than 25 MB, created only if separately approved.
expected result: UNVERIFIED REQUIREMENT: UI text says up to 25MB, but inspected dropzone has no maxSize and backend checks extension only; agree on size policy before any upload.

scenario: Compare filename extension and declared content type
steps: In isolated QA, submit a harmless text fixture with an allowed extension and a mismatched declared content type.
test data: Synthetic non-sensitive text; no executable content.
expected result: UNVERIFIED REQUIREMENT: code visibly chooses allowed extensions from filename and uses content_type for extraction; no explicit content-signature validation was found; define expected policy first.

scenario: Try to list documents using a department outside the user's scope
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and request GET /api/v1/upload/documents?department=UnknownQADept.
test data: Unique department value different from the authenticated user's department.
expected result: The request is rejected with HTTP 403; a caller-supplied filter cannot broaden the authenticated scope.

scenario: Delete an existing disposable document in the user's department
steps: Authenticate as a QA user, upload a document in that account's department, capture its id, then DELETE /api/v1/upload/document/{id}.
test data: Disposable QA document id and valid bearer token.
expected result: Response should report successful deletion and the same id; do not run against non-test records.

scenario: Delete an id that does not exist
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and DELETE /api/v1/upload/document/{unused-id}.
test data: Unused positive integer in isolated QA database and valid bearer token.
expected result: Route should return HTTP 404 with detail Document not found.

scenario: Check file, database record, and vector chunks after authorized deletion
steps: Authenticate as a QA user; upload a uniquely named fixture in the account's department; record returned id and file path; delete it; check file, database, list, and search results.
test data: Disposable file, valid bearer token, and corresponding returned document id.
expected result: Route attempts all cleanup steps after department authorization; verify physical file absent, DB row absent, and matching chunks absent separately. Record any cleanup error; do not infer unobserved success.

scenario: Omit required search query
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and GET /api/v1/search/ without a query parameter.
test data: Valid bearer token; no query parameter.
expected result: FastAPI should reject missing required query with HTTP 422.

scenario: Search indexed QA content in the authenticated department
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and GET /api/v1/search/?query={distinctive fixture text}.
test data: Valid bearer token; text from TC-024 indexed in the user's department in the same backend process.
expected result: Response includes query, authenticated department, and vector results; service requests top_k=5. Exact ranking is not specified.

scenario: Search within the authenticated user's department
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and search without a filter or with the user's department.
test data: Matching synthetic documents indexed in the user's department.
expected result: Search is constrained to the authenticated user's department; returned department metadata must not include another department.

scenario: Search using a department outside the authenticated scope
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and call search with a different department filter.
test data: User and indexed fixtures in distinct synthetic departments.
expected result: The request is rejected and does not return results from the requested other department.

scenario: Submit an authenticated question through GET RAG endpoint
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and GET /api/v1/rag/?query={question about indexed fixture}.
test data: Valid bearer token; synthetic indexed QA document in the user's department and matching question.
expected result: Route passes query and authenticated department to the RAG generator and returns its response; exact generated answer is not specified.

scenario: Submit an authenticated question through POST RAG endpoint
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and POST JSON with query to /api/v1/rag/.
test data: Valid bearer token; synthetic indexed QA document in the user's department and a matching query.
expected result: Route passes query and authenticated department to the RAG generator and returns response data; exact generated wording is not specified.

scenario: Omit query from POST RAG body
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and POST JSON without query to /api/v1/rag/.
test data: Valid bearer token; JSON body without query.
expected result: Pydantic request model requires query; FastAPI should reject with HTTP 422.

scenario: Ask a question when the QA vector collection has no matching chunks
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and POST a query before indexing any QA document in the fresh isolated vector collection.
test data: Valid bearer token; fresh QA vector collection and unrelated query.
expected result: Code returns the no-relevant-knowledge answer with empty retrieved_chunks and sources; execution remains unmeasured.

scenario: Ask a question matching an indexed QA document
steps: Authenticate as a QA user; upload a synthetic fixture in that user's department, then POST a matching query to RAG using the same process.
test data: Valid bearer token; synthetic text containing a unique fact.
expected result: For retrieved chunks, code builds an answer and sources from chunk metadata; inspect answer and citations against returned chunks without assuming wording or a grounding threshold.

scenario: Inspect citation metadata for a retrieved chunk
steps: Authenticate as a QA user, run a matching RAG query within the user's department, and inspect each returned source object.
test data: Valid bearer token; fixture with known filename, document id, and department.
expected result: Source builder includes filename, document_id, department, and snippet fields with fallback metadata where needed.

scenario: Inspect long source snippets
steps: Authenticate as a QA user, index a synthetic chunk longer than 200 characters in that user's department, and request it through RAG.
test data: Valid bearer token; synthetic long text with no confidential data.
expected result: Source builder uses the first 200 characters and appends three dots when longer, producing a 203-character snippet; verify actual value.

scenario: Retrieve multiple chunks from the same document
steps: Authenticate as a QA user, index a QA document with multiple matching chunks in that user's department, and send a matching RAG query.
test data: Valid bearer token; one synthetic multi-chunk document.
expected result: Code deduplicates sources by filename and document_id; retrieved_chunks can still contain multiple chunks.

scenario: Ask for content outside the authenticated user's department
steps: Authenticate as a QA user and send a RAG request with a conflicting department value.
test data: Synthetic cross-department fixtures and a valid QA token.
expected result: The request is rejected and does not return an answer or citations derived from another department.

scenario: Check whether answer claims are supported by retrieved content
steps: Ask questions with known and absent facts against a small synthetic corpus; compare each factual claim to returned chunks.
test data: Synthetic corpus with one known fact and one deliberately absent fact.
expected result: UNVERIFIED REQUIREMENT: prompt requests answers using only context, but no measurable grounding threshold or guarantee exists in inspected code; define review rubric before pass/fail.

scenario: Inspect chat network response for streaming behavior
steps: Send a chat question and inspect response headers/body in browser network tools or API client.
test data: Synthetic QA query; isolated backend.
expected result: UNVERIFIED: no SSE/StreamingResponse/EventSource implementation was found in inspected application source; current RAG routes return generator output as regular route responses; do not expect SSE without a feature requirement.

scenario: Submit a password shorter than the frontend minimum directly to signup
steps: In isolated QA, POST signup with a valid email/name and a short password; do not use a real account.
test data: Disposable identity; short synthetic password.
expected result: UNVERIFIED product policy: frontend requires six characters, while backend UserCreate declares password as str without a visible minimum; confirm desired backend behavior before pass/fail.

scenario: Check browser preflight for configured test origin
steps: Start only an approved isolated QA backend with ALLOWED_ORIGINS set to a test origin; send OPTIONS preflight for a QA request.
test data: Local QA origin and harmless request headers.
expected result: CORS middleware derives allowed_origins from configuration and adds local origins; verify actual response headers; no run performed.

scenario: Compare summary to known QA records
steps: GET /api/v1/stats/summary after creating known QA users/documents.
test data: Small known set with Processed and non-Processed document records.
expected result: Counts should follow route queries and recent_documents should include up to five latest ids; compare against exact QA fixture set.

scenario: Plan response-time measurement for health endpoint
steps: After a product owner defines target and sample size, record repeated health-request durations and summarize percentile values.
test data: Isolated QA environment; <APPROVED TARGET>; <APPROVED SAMPLE SIZE>.
expected result: UNVERIFIED requirement: no latency target or benchmark result exists in repository evidence; record measurements only after an approved run.

scenario: Plan measurement for document processing latency
steps: After defining file sizes and target, time uploads of synthetic PDF/TXT/DOCX fixtures and record extraction/indexing completion.
test data: Isolated QA backend; synthetic files; <APPROVED FILE SIZES>; <APPROVED TARGET>.
expected result: UNVERIFIED requirement: no upload-time target or measurement is present; no performance claim can be made before execution.

scenario: Plan search/RAG response-time measurement
steps: After warm-up and target definition, issue repeated semantic-search and RAG requests against a fixed synthetic corpus and record percentiles separately.
test data: Isolated QA vector collection; <APPROVED CORPUS SIZE>; <APPROVED TARGET>.
expected result: UNVERIFIED requirement: no retrieval/RAG latency target or measurement exists; report observations without inventing a pass threshold.

scenario: Plan controlled concurrency evaluation
steps: Only after approving a concurrency profile and isolated capacity, issue the agreed number of simultaneous read-only health/search requests and capture errors and latency.
test data: Isolated QA environment; <APPROVED CONCURRENCY>; <APPROVED DURATION>.
expected result: UNVERIFIED requirement: no concurrency target or capacity claim exists; do not run until profile and environment are approved.

scenario: Check core screens in Chrome
steps: After agreeing supported versions, open login, dashboard, documents, and chat in Chrome and record rendering and core interactions.
test data: Approved Chrome version; synthetic account and QA fixtures.
expected result: UNVERIFIED requirement: repository names no supported-browser matrix; capture observations but do not declare compatibility until versions and acceptance criteria are agreed.

scenario: Check core screens in Edge
steps: After agreeing supported versions, open login, dashboard, documents, and chat in Edge and record rendering and core interactions.
test data: Approved Edge version; synthetic account and QA fixtures.
expected result: UNVERIFIED requirement: repository names no supported-browser matrix; capture observations but do not declare compatibility until versions and acceptance criteria are agreed.

scenario: Check core screens in Firefox
steps: After agreeing supported versions, open login, dashboard, documents, and chat in Firefox and record rendering and core interactions.
test data: Approved Firefox version; synthetic account and QA fixtures.
expected result: UNVERIFIED requirement: repository names no supported-browser matrix; capture observations but do not declare compatibility until versions and acceptance criteria are agreed.

scenario: Check chat and document controls at narrow viewport
steps: At an approved mobile-width viewport, inspect chat input/scope controls and document upload/filter controls; exercise core interactions.
test data: Approved viewport dimensions and browser; synthetic fixtures.
expected result: Responsive styles and separate mobile chat controls exist, but no viewport/browser acceptance matrix is documented; define supported sizes before pass/fail.
